incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: service=redwood-inference-prod routing_key=svc-rl-prod-01 — urgency=high — reason=High error rate on inference runtime

pagerduty-bot: paging emma (oncall) via schedule 'prod-sre-main' (rule: immediate) — escalation policy: prod-escalation-v2

emma (oncall): got it, ack'ing now. Looking at logs

emma (oncall): acked — I see a spike in 5xx from runtime-gpu-01 around 11:12 UTC, correlates with a deploy?

devon (sre): which deploy? I don't see any deploy notes in the deploy-bot channel. Can you paste the error sample?

emma (oncall): stacktrace snippet: `2024-06-04T11:12:03Z error: kvcache miss -> OOM while allocating 512MB for attention cache`

sam (eng): oh — that looks like a kernel change we rolled last night on Dedicated pools for continuous batching. Could be config mismatch on small-instance pool.

emma (oncall): paging note: PagerDuty routed to prod-sre-main schedule but the person listed as primary was a contractor (kevin) — he got paged but his schedule is only for shadow pages. I wasn't expecting that.

kevin (ops): I did get a page and forwarded to emma — I don't have permissions on the Dedicated pool to restart nodes.

maria (support): we're getting inbound Zendesk tickets complaining about timeouts in customer apps. Multiple customers in EU region. Estimated impacted customers: 3 paying accounts.

emma (oncall): ok triage plan: 1) confirm if kernel change caused new memory growth 2) fallback: disable continuous batching on the small-instance pool 3) if that fails, switch routing to fallback model variant (cpu-safe) to stop customer errors

devon (sre): Emma — can you confirm who PagerDuty actually escalated to? The escalation logs show a shadow schedule binding leaked into prod-escalation-v2. This looks like a routing rule that picks schedule by alias instead of schedule_id.

emma (oncall): checking PD audit... yes, policy targeted `schedule_alias: prod-sre` which currently resolves to two schedules: prod-sre-main and prod-sre-shadow. prod-sre-shadow has kevin as primary. That explains the contractor page.

sam (eng): ugh. We recently added alias mapping to make oncall rotations easier but didn't lock who resolves aliases. We should always pin to schedule_id in escalation policies.

kevin (ops): temporary mitigation: I can rebind the alias to only include prod-sre-main for now. Want me to do that?

emma (oncall): yes please, do that and confirm. Also please add a note in PD: "temp: shadow removed from prod alias after live incident"

pagerduty-bot: change applied by kevin (ops): `alias prod-sre -> [prod-sre-main]` — audit id pd-audit-7832

maria (support): forwarding customers with ETA 30m for mitigation to affected accounts. I'll add status updates: "We're investigating increased timeouts, mitigation in progress."

devon (sre): on the runtime side I'm seeing kernel allocations spike after request #128 from batcher. Sam, can you roll back the kernel tweak on the small-instance pool? If not, disable continuous batching on those hosts.

sam (eng): initiating rollback on pool small-instance-1 -> rolling back to previous kernel build (cmd: `deploy rollback --pool small-instance-1 --to 20240602-kernel-v3`)

emma (oncall): confirming: after alias change, future pages should go to prod-sre-main only. Also manually re-routed the active alert to emma.

incident-bot: alert re-routed to emma (oncall) — previous ack by kevin (ops) remains in audit.

kevin (ops): kernel rollback succeeded on one host, others still pending. I don't have permission to trigger full autoscale reboot.

sam (eng): triggering disable of continuous batching on small-instance-1: `runtimectl set-config small-instance-1 --continuous_batching=false`

sam (eng): done on all hosts in pool. Observed immediate drop in 5xxs on metrics.

emma (oncall): 11:28 UTC — 5xx count down from 320/min to ~10/min. Latency back to normal for affected customers. Maria, please update customers that mitigation applied and we're monitoring.

maria (support): doing that now. Also scheduling a follow-up call with the three affected accounts to offer a post-incident writeup.

devon (sre): root cause summary so far: alias-based scheduling allowed shadow schedule to be part of prod escalation; kernel change + continuous batching memory pattern triggered OOMs on small-instance pool. Immediate fixes: rebind alias to prod-sre-main, disable continuous batching on small-instance pool, rollback kernel where needed.

emma (oncall): opening incident doc and assigning action items: `INC-2024-06-04-pd-routing-fanout` — owners: sam (rollback verification), devon (postmortem), kevin (PD escalation config), maria (customer comms). ETA for postmortem draft: 48h.

kevin (ops): I'll update PD escalation policies to reference schedule_id instead of alias and add a validation check to CI for new PD config changes.

sam (eng): will add a canary for continuous batching kernel builds on a non-production pool next rollout.

emma (oncall): thanks all. Closing incident thread — continuing work in the incident doc. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident marked resolved by emma (oncall) — duration ~18m — customers impacted: 3 accounts — severity: Sev2
